citeAs: Merity, Stephen, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, and Richard Socher. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv.
creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher (Salesforce)
description: A freely available language modeling corpus constructed from Wikipedia articles. It is released in two sizes, WikiText-2 and WikiText-103, and preserves article structure, punctuation, original casing, and a much larger vocabulary than Penn Treebank to support modeling of rare words and long-range dependencies.
name: WikiText
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is restricted to Wikipedia articles rated Good or Featured by editors, which are described as reviewed by humans and considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. This curation choice biases the corpus toward higher-quality, editor-selected Wikipedia content.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed from Wikipedia by selecting articles that met Wikipedia's Good or Featured article criteria, then extracting each article's text using the Wikipedia API.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data consisted of Wikipedia articles, specifically 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles, extracted from Wikipedia markup via the Wikipedia API.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper motivates WikiText as an improvement over Penn Treebank but does note design choices such as replacing mathematical formulae and LaTeX code with <formula> tokens, removing sections primarily featuring lists, and using only articles meeting Good or Featured article criteria.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was released in two sizes, WikiText-2 and WikiText-103. Validation and test use the same articles in both, while vocabularies differ by dataset size. A vocabulary cutoff was applied by discarding words with count below 3 and mapping remaining out-of-vocabulary words to the <unk> token.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: After extraction, sections primarily featuring lists were removed by default; leaked HTML artifacts such as sort keys and Edit buttons were removed; mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens; normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, augmented to further split numbers; and a vocabulary was built by discarding all words with count below 3, mapping out-of-vocabulary words to the <unk> token.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended as a benchmark dataset for language modeling, especially for evaluating handling of rare words, realistic vocabularies, and long-range dependencies.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Wikipedia API for article extraction; Moses tokenizer for normalization and tokenization.
